cellLabel: {c} equals {v}. Press to see how it is computed
sizeRule: ({l}) · ({r}) gives a ({o}) matrix: the columns of the first and the rows of the second match and disappear.
whySumSize: They cannot be added: A is {a} and B is {b}. To add, both matrices must have the same size.
whyProductSize: They cannot be multiplied in this order: {left} has {c} columns and {right} has {r} rows. To multiply, the columns of the first must equal the rows of the second ({ls} times {rs}).
whyBadScalar: Type a valid number for λ to see the result.
cellHint: Press another entry of the result. In a product, the row of the first matrix and the column of the second are highlighted; they are multiplied in pairs and added up.
cellNone: Press an entry of the result to see how it is computed.
orderHint: With numbers, 2 · 3 = 3 · 2. With matrices not always: the product is not commutative.
order_neither: Neither AB nor BA exists: the columns of A are not the rows of B, nor the other way round.
order_onlyAB: AB exists but BA does not: B has {bc} columns and A has {ar} rows.
order_onlyBA: BA exists but AB does not: A has {ac} columns and B has {br} rows.
order_sizes: AB is {ab} and BA is {ba}: they have different sizes, so they cannot be equal.
order_equal: AB = BA: these two matrices commute (a special case, not the rule).
order_differ: AB ≠ BA: for example, at {c} one gives {x} and the other {y}.
traceNeedSquare: The trace only exists for square matrices, and {name} is not one.
traceProducts: tr(AB) = {ab} and tr(BA) = {ba}: they always agree, even when AB ≠ BA.
traceProductsNone: To compare tr(AB) with tr(BA) you need two matrices whose sizes fit in both orders, such as 2 × 3 and 3 × 2.
